answers.flag: Option B says SSE-C is allowed in the bucket's default encryption settings, but SSE-C is chosen per request and is not a default-encryption option, so a careful candidate could call B technically wrong and A (the only other option where S3 encrypts with a key held outside AWS) defensible.

case.label: A
case.text: A also keeps the key outside AWS and has S3 encrypt and decrypt with the customer-supplied key (SSE-C), and the client-side encryption step only adds protection; if B's claim that SSE-C is a bucket default setting is read as inaccurate, A is the only option whose wording is not wrong about the S3 feature, and the stem never says that double encryption is forbidden.

case.label: A
case.text: The stem allows up to 24 hours for an archived log but does not name the retrieval tier; if a candidate worries that Deep Archive bulk retrieval can take longer than 24 hours, S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval (whose standard and bulk tiers both finish within hours) looks like the safer fit for the 24-hour limit, and Deep Archive's 180-day minimum and per-GB retrieval fees can be read as risks. This is weak because the standard tier of Deep Archive fits 24 hours and A costs more per GB-month, and the cue 'only copy' plus 'milliseconds' mainly rules out B and C.
